name: Public lewdness (intercourse; ordinary)
conduct: Knowingly engaging in sexual intercourse: penetration of the female sex organ by the male sex organ, under the statutory definition. The act must occur in a public place or, if not public, the actor must be reckless about whether another person is present who will be offended or alarmed. Private consensual conduct without that statutory circumstance is not automatically public lewdness. A public place is one to which the public or a substantial group has access. This ordinary branch excludes an actor civilly committed as a sexually violent predator under Chapter 841, for whom §21.07(b) provides third-degree grading.
penalty: Class A misdemeanor: ordinarily up to one year in jail, a fine up to $4,000, or both. The civil-commitment enhancement applies to conduct on or after September 1, 2023; if any element occurred before that date, the then-applicable law governs. Other repeat or sentencing findings require separate analysis.

Other repeat or sentencing findings require separate analysis.

name: Indecent exposure (anus; ordinary)
conduct: Exposing the anus with intent to arouse or gratify any person’s sexual desire, while reckless about whether another person is present who will be offended or alarmed. Mere nudity, or exposure without both the specific intent and recklessness, does not by itself establish this offense. A public place is not a statutory requirement. This ordinary branch has no prior §21.08 conviction and excludes a civilly committed sexually violent predator.
penalty: Class B misdemeanor: ordinarily up to 180 days in jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both. The one-prior and two-or-more-prior grades (H.B. 1730) and the civil-commitment grade (S.B. 1179) apply to offenses committed on or after September 1, 2023. S.B. 1610 reenacted the combined text effective September 1, 2025. If any element occurred before September 1, 2023, earlier law governs; the charging date alone does not determine the applicable grade. A second §21.08 violation is a reportable conviction under Code of Criminal Procedure article 62.001(5)(F), except if that second violation results in deferred adjudication; registration duties and duration require the applicable Chapter 62 analysis. Other repeat or sentencing findings require separate analysis.

name: Indecent assault (touch; ordinary)
conduct: Touching another person’s anus, breast or genitals. The conduct must be without the other person’s consent and with intent to arouse or gratify any person’s sexual desire. Neither contact alone nor an unconsented act without that sexual intent establishes this section. This ordinary branch excludes a prior conviction under this section and the qualifying treatment-provider circumstances. These choices cover the common grading text retained in both 2025 versions of subsection (b). They exclude an elderly individual (65 or older), a disabled individual as defined in §22.04(c), and the qualifying civil-commitment-facility officer/employee/contractor circumstances described in the other (b)(3). Those special scenarios can carry higher grades and need their own assessment; they are not treated as ordinary misdemeanors here. If the same conduct violates another criminal law, §22.012(c) permits prosecution under this section, the other law, or both; this choice does not displace child-specific or other sexual-offense statutes.
penalty: Class A misdemeanor: ordinarily up to one year in jail, a fine up to $4,000, or both. The prior/provider enhancements were enacted effective September 1, 2023; if any element occurred before that date, earlier law governs. Both retained special (b)(3) amendments apply prospectively from September 1, 2025 with the same any-element transition. Other sentencing enhancements and registration consequences require separate assessment.
